result:
I fixed the 9 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings. A brute-force check over many quantities and unit prices now finds no rule that differs from its docstring or the module docstring's shared rules.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02 | Gave 4% off instead of 3% | Changed to 3% |
| 27 | Applied the cap to the price, not the discount | Cap now applies to the discount |
| 54 | Gave 8% off instead of 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 67 | Rounded the discount with `round` instead of rounding down | Now rounds down (`//`) |
| 72 | Gave 6% off instead of 5% | Changed to 5% |
| 128 | The 50,000 won cap only kicked in once the discount passed 100,000 | Cap now always applies |
| 142 | Same as 128 | Cap now always applies |
| 145 | Applied the cap to the price, not the discount | Cap now applies to the discount |
| 146 | Used `qty > 12`, so exactly 12 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 12` |

Rules 32, 105 and 106 look odd: they use `>= 13` or `> N` instead of `>= N`. They're "marginal" rules, though, so at exactly the threshold the discount is 0 anyway and the result is the same. I left them as they were.

STATUS: DONE
